compile.summary: FP32 engine built in 8.2s — 199 TRT layers, 18.6 MB.
compile.detail:
**best.onnx → best.fp32.plan**  ·  TensorRT 10.3.0

The engine is on disk and this is the file that gets deployed. Nothing has been run yet, so none of this is a speed measurement — the build time above is how long it took to CREATE, not how fast it goes.

**Built at FP32, and every layer stayed there.** Nothing fell back.

**Layout conversion — 21% of layers**

41 of 199 layers do no maths. They only rearrange data so the next layer can read it.

Around 8% is normal at FP32. What this number is really for is comparing two builds of the SAME model: a jump after a precision change is the cost of extra shuffling, not a worse choice of kernel. At 21% a large share of this engine is moving data rather than computing — worth comparing against another precision before concluding the model is simply expensive.

**What the engine is made of**

| Kind | Count | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| CaskConvolution | 70 | convolutions |
| PointWiseV2 | 69 | elementwise maths, fused |
| Reformat | 41 | layout/precision conversion — overhead, not maths |
| NoOp | 8 | removed entirely |
| Constant | 3 | — |
| CaskPooling | 3 | — |
| Resize | 2 | resizing |
| Shuffle | 2 | reshapes and transposes |
| CaskSoftMaxV2 | 1 | — |

These are TensorRT's own kernel families, after it merged what it could — which is why the count does not match the ONNX node count.
warnings: First build on this GPU, so every kernel had to be timed (8s). The timings are now cached; rebuilding this model after surgery or quantization will be far quicker.

**mAP@0.5 0.0000 against COCO 2017 validation slice (30 samples) ground truth (unchanged vs the ONNX on the same data) · 30 sample(s)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Measured against | COCO 2017 validation slice (30 samples) ground truth |
| Samples | 30 |
| Engine | `best.fp32.plan` |
| Reference | `best.onnx` (FP32 ONNX) |

| Metric | Engine | ONNX | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| mAP@0.5 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | +0.0000 |
| mAP@0.5:0.95 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | +0.0000 |
| Precision@0.5 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | +0.0000 |
| Recall@0.5 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | +0.0000 |
| Predictions | 25 | 25 | +0.0000 |
| Ground-truth objects | 296 | 296 | +0.0000 |

**What these mean**

- **mAP@0.5** — Mean average precision at IoU 0.5 — the standard detection score. Charges for missed objects and for false positives, which a box-overlap average cannot.
- **mAP@0.5:0.95** — Averaged over ten IoU thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95. Stricter: it moves when box coordinates drift, not only when detections are lost.
- **Precision@0.5** — Of everything the model reported, how much was real.
- **Recall@0.5** — Of everything that was there, how much it found.
- **Predictions** — Total detections reported across the set.
- **Ground-truth objects** — Total objects the labels contain.
